full_description: Learn to transform prepared 3D architectural scenes into convincing visual presentations. Develop practical control over V-Ray materials, realistic daylight and artificial lighting, camera exposure, global illumination and rendering quality. required: Working Autodesk 3ds Max modeling knowledge (viewport navigation, object organization, basic materials, scene scale, opening scenes) OR completion of Course 74 (3ds Max Architectural Modeling & Visualization)

Chaos V-Ray for 3ds Max installed (stable release v6–v7)
NVIDIA GPU with CUDA/RTX support if utilizing V-Ray GPU compute features
Adobe Photoshop / Camera Raw (or compatible image editor) for presentation layouts and post-processing

highlights: 6 Weeks of focused photorealistic rendering specialization (48 guided learning hours)
Master Chaos V-Ray for Autodesk 3ds Max interface, physical materials, and render setup

V-Ray Frame Buffer (VFB) layers, LightMix interactive lighting adjustments, and render elements

learning_outcomes: Configure V-Ray as the production and interactive renderer in Autodesk 3ds Max.
Understand physically based rendering principles and light transport mechanics.
Organize scenes, external asset paths, and texture dependencies cleanly using Asset Tracking.
Distinguish between V-Ray CPU and GPU workflows, selecting the appropriate engine based on hardware.
Verify renderer compatibility, memory limitations, and hardware requirements.
Build realistic V-Ray materials using the VRayMtl shader and Slate Material Editor.
Control reflections, refractions, roughness, index of refraction (IOR), and Fresnel response accurately.
Use bump, normal, and introductory displacement maps with proper data interpretation.
Apply appropriate texture and UV scale to architectural surfaces using UVW Map coordinates.
Configure V-Ray Sun and Sky systems for realistic architectural daylight scenarios.
Set up HDRI and dome lighting for accurate environmental reflections and natural illumination.
Create realistic artificial interior lighting using V-Ray area lights, spheres, and IES photometric profiles.
Control physical camera exposure using ISO, f-number, shutter speed, and white balance.
Develop consistent day and night lighting treatments for the same architectural space.
Understand global illumination (GI) with primary (Brute Force) and secondary (Light Cache) bounces.
Interpret render noise and sampling behavior to distinguish between shadow, reflection, and GI noise.
Configure suitable denoising workflows (V-Ray Denoiser, NVIDIA AI) with detail-preservation checks.
Diagnose and resolve common render problems such as light leaks, color bleeding, and GPU memory limits.
Work effectively with the V-Ray Frame Buffer (VFB) interface, layers, history, and comparison tools.
Use LightMix to adjust light intensities, colors, and mood variations interactively without re-rendering.
Understand render elements (passes) and basic Cryptomatte mask extraction workflows.
Apply colour-management principles, linear workflows, and display transforms.
Prepare client-ready render outputs in appropriate bit depths and delivery formats (PNG, JPG, EXR).
Document rendering settings, optimization observations, and hardware metrics systematically.
Package editable 3ds Max scene files, materials, and linked assets for seamless studio handover.

faq.question: Is this V-Ray course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: This is an intermediate specialization. Working 3ds Max knowledge is recommended. Students without that background should complete Course 74 (3ds Max Architectural Modeling & Visualization) first.

faq.question: What will I learn?
faq.answer: You will learn V-Ray materials, PBR textures, architectural lighting, cameras, global illumination, sampling, denoising, V-Ray Frame Buffer, LightMix, and professional image finishing.

faq.question: Do I need 3ds Max before learning V-Ray?
faq.answer: Yes. The course uses V-Ray for Autodesk 3ds Max, so you should understand basic 3ds Max scene navigation, modeling, and organization.

faq.question: Will I learn photorealistic interior rendering?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn material realism, natural and artificial lighting, camera exposure, GI, and final image finishing for interior scenes.

faq.question: Will I learn exterior rendering?
faq.answer: Yes. The course includes architectural exterior visualization with controlled daylight, shadows, materials, and camera composition.

faq.question: What portfolio will I create?
faq.answer: You will prepare an interior render, an exterior render, two lighting treatments of one scene, and a technical rendering breakdown containing material tests, LightMix evidence, and render settings.

faq.question: Do I need to model every object?
faq.answer: No. This is a rendering specialization. Students may use supplied, previously modeled (Course 74), or properly licensed scenes and assets.

faq.question: Will I learn V-Ray GPU?
faq.answer: Yes. The course introduces CPU and GPU rendering, compatibility considerations, hardware requirements, and realistic performance optimization.

faq.question: Does GPU rendering always produce faster results?
faq.answer: No. Performance depends on hardware, scene complexity, available memory, settings, and feature support.

faq.question: Will I learn LightMix?
faq.answer: Yes. The course teaches V-Ray Frame Buffer, LightMix, and controlled lighting variations without re-rendering.

faq.question: Will I learn V-Ray denoising?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn available denoising workflows, quality checks, and common artifacts. Denoising is not a substitute for correct sampling and lighting.

faq.question: Will I learn real-time V-Ray rendering?
faq.answer: The course introduces modern interactive rendering and explains optional integrated real-time viewport workflows where the required software and licensing are available.

faq.question: Is Chaos Vantage included?
faq.answer: Chaos Vantage is not included by default unless you possess an active V-Ray Collection or Vantage license. The course teaches Vantage as an optional workflow, while ensuring all core certification projects are fully achievable using standard V-Ray.

faq.question: Is V-Ray free?
faq.answer: Chaos V-Ray is commercial software. Student, educational, trial, and commercial subscription access depend on applicable Chaos licensing terms.

faq.question: Does the course include Twinmotion walkthroughs?
faq.answer: No. This course focuses on photorealistic rendering and image finishing. Real-time walkthroughs and animated presentations are covered separately in Course 76.

faq.question: Will I receive editable project files?
faq.answer: Students are required to prepare editable 3ds Max scenes, organized materials, render settings, final images, and technical handover documentation.

faq.question: What is the duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course lasts six weeks, includes 48 guided learning hours, and has a listed fee of ₹8,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.
